subject: Draft MAP: technical evaluation milestones & benchmark targets
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-12T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Draft MAP: technical evaluation milestones & benchmark targets

Thanks again for the intro call today — appreciated the clarity on HealthGrid's timeline and constraints. As promised, attaching an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the technical evaluation milestone we discussed. High-level recap and proposed owner/responsibility split below:

- Objective: Complete technical evaluation for inference integration and confirm model selection by target close date.
- Target close date for MAP milestone: 2025-12-19 (approx. 5 weeks)

Proposed Milestones (owner in parens):
1) Benchmarks defined & test harness ready (HealthGrid + Redwood SRE) — target 2025-11-20
2) Latency & cost baseline run on representative load (Redwood + HealthGrid infra) — target 2025-11-27
3) Model shortlist & qualitative review (HealthGrid ML + Redwood SE) — target 2025-12-03
4) Final selection and rollout plan (joint) — target 2025-12-19

Key success criteria I suggest for the benchmarks:
- P95 latency under 150ms for 256-token requests (90% of test cases)
- Average inference cost per 1k tokens under $0.60 on dedicated setup (post-quantization)
- No regression in response coherence for our standard eval prompts (baseline pass rate >= 92%)

Dependencies and blockers:
- Access to a representative sample dataset and 3 test endpoints (HealthGrid infra).
- Temporary service account and short-lived credentials for KV/cache profiling.

Next steps:
- Camila will draft the test harness template and latency/cost matrix (I asked her to include a template sheet).
- Maya — can you confirm who on your side owns providing the sample dataset and whether procurement needs any formal request?

Attachment: MAP_draft_v1.pdf (high-level timeline)

If that aligns, I'll drop these milestones into HubSpot and set reminders for the checkpoints.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes

Thanks, Rafael — good summary and thanks for the quick turnaround on the MAP. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can own the sample dataset delivery. I'll have Luke package a redacted sample and the access instructions by 2025-11-18.
- Procurement: we do not need a formal PO for the evaluation lab, but our security team will require an NDA + short questionnaire before we share service accounts. I copied procurement here.
- Success criteria: the latency targets look reasonable, but our internal ops team uses P99 in production for SLA assessments. Can we add a P99 check (target < 250ms) for the final run?

One ask: can you confirm whether the cost target is for hosted Redwood or for a dedicated reserved setup? We want apples-to-apples numbers for our internal TCO exercise.

Thanks — Maya

Subject: Re: Draft MAP: technical evaluation milestones & benchmark targets

Hi all — Camila here (SE). I put together a technical-eval plan and attached two artifacts: latency_bench_template.xlsx and model_shortlist_notes.md. Below is a condensed plan and how we'll run the benchmark.

Plan summary:
- Environment: We'll run three phases — (A) Redwood hosted sandbox for quick iteration, (B) Dedicated reserved pool simulation (quantized weights) for throughput/cost estimates, (C) On-prem/VPC smoke test if HealthGrid requests.
- Workload: 1) Synthetic steady-state stream (50 RPS, 256-token avg). 2) Burst profile (250 RPS spike for 1 minute). 3) Long-sequence evaluation (1024 tokens for a subset).
- Metrics collected: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, cost-per-1k-tokens (estimated), and qualitative correctness pass rate (our eval set).

Success thresholds (suggested):
- P95 < 150ms (steady-state, 256 tokens)
- P99 < 250ms (steady-state) — added per Maya's note
- Burst tail: 95th percentile of burst requests < 400ms
- Cost: hosted sandbox (informational). Dedicated sim: cost <= $0.60 per 1k tokens after quantization for the production-like profile
- Quality: automated eval pass >= 92% on the provided prompt suite

Model shortlist (initial candidate set):
- Mistral-7B (quantized) — high throughput, lower cost
- Llama2-13B (int8) — quality baseline, medium cost
- OpenRedwood-3B (redwood-curated) — fast KV/cache performance

What I need from HealthGrid to proceed:
- Sample dataset and 3 representative request endpoints (API endpoints or a description of client request patterns).
- Confirmation whether we should include on-prem step (adds 3–5 business days to schedule).

I can run a dry benchmark on hosted sandbox within 48 hours of receiving the sample dataset. I'll also push the benchmark results into the shared Drive folder and tag the HubSpot deal.

Attachment: latency_bench_template.xlsx (sheet with workload and metric columns)
Attachment: model_shortlist_notes.md

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
